title.narrative: Locally Led Integrated flood and other emergency response through proactive, inclusive and community driven approach in Northeast Nigeria.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Future Resilience and Development Foundation (FRAD Foundation) in partnership with Smiling Heart Initiative International (SHI) proposes a 6-month anticipatory action project aimed at proactively addressing immediate and predictable impacts of flood and other natural disasters In the BAY state. The project will fosters an inclusive approach that focuses on averting disease outbreaks, reducing displacement, protecting livelihoods, and alleviating pressure on already overstretched humanitarian resources through early warning systems, pre-positioning of emergency supplies, community sensitization and proactive interventions, FRAD and SHI under the Project hope to mitigate the worst possible impact of flooding and other hazards in conflict affected communities in the BAY state. lt/pgtltpgtThe project will Be focusing primarily targeting two areas of Food security using multi-purpose cash assistance that provides beneficiaries dignity and self-reliance in managing their needs during emergencies. The project will also be using a holistic approach to reduce displacement, protect livelihood and properties through coordinated approach for CCCM, This approach will be ensured through pre flooding simulation activities at the flood prone communities, identification of safe relocation sites to reduce protection risk of affected communities during emergency, prepositioning of camp kits and other camp management settings to ensure immediate activations when anticipator triggers occur.lt/pgtltpgtFRAD and SHI will be deploying innovations promote reduction of vulnerabilities caused by displacement through key areas.ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtUse MPCA to Provide dignified means to immediate food security needs of affected Households within 3 days of occurrence of the displacement/emergencies using the Minimum expenditure basket for food security per household.lt/ligtltligtUse of Simulation exercise with community structures and Government to pre plan to reduce risk and vulnerabilities during flooding and other emergencies.lt/ligtltligtPrepositioning of CCCM mitigation kits, identification of key camp management personnel for immediate deployment during emergencies.lt/ligtltligtUse of multi-sectoral coordinated approach to response thereby increasing quality of service and reducing duplication. lt/ligtltligtCoordination with relevant agencies to provide temporary assistance/shelter and protection to people displaced from their homes.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtTo promote protection of affected population, the consortium (FRAD and SHI) will ensure Mainstreaming of protection, AAP, safeguarding and disability inclusion to ensure that further harm is not caused as a result of the work we do, and vulnerable populations like Persons with disability are not excluded during the intervention. Through the project approach, FRAD and SHI seeks to improve access to basic household needs as well as immediate life-saving assistance like food. Early warning system of flood awareness, cholera prevention as well as camp coordination, ensuring a robust referral mechanism that allows for enhanced support to affected people.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project targets flood prone communities in Adamawa state FRAD will implement in ltbgtYola North, Yola South, lt/bgtwhile SHI will implement CCCM activities inltspangtltbgt, Yola North, Yola South, Fufure and Gireilt/bgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtlt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project Theory of Change islt/pgtltpgtIF vulnerable communities are supported through anticipatory interventions including timely multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA), strengthened site coordination (CCCM) and community preparedness measures THEN they will be able to act early, reduce displacement, prevent disease outbreaks, and meet their priority needs with dignity,ltbrgtwithin 24 Hours of emergency. ltbrgtlt/pgt
